title: But what is a Fourier series? From heat flow to drawing with circles | DE4
beats: Opens with 300 rotating arrows drawing a shape; each arrow trivial, the sum anything but
Formula is short; start with real sine waves (Fourier's origin), generalize later; prior videos optional
Heat equation recap: cosine waves decay exponentially, faster at high frequency
Linearity: add and scale solutions to get dials for custom initial conditions
Step function from two rods is nothing like waves; Fourier asks the absurd question anyway
Objection: finite sums are only approximations; infinite sum needed
Infinite sum of fractions to pi/4 as a model of limits; functions do it pointwise in parallel
Value at jump forced to 0; analysis nuances swept under rug and linked out
Real challenge is finding coefficients; generalize to complex outputs as drawings
Function as pencil tip tracing a path; real functions are boring 1D drawings
Pairs of opposite-rotating vectors give a sine wave; Fourier's case is the special case
e^(it) walks the unit circle; can be treated as shorthand but is more than that
Rotating vector e^(n 2 pi i t), integer n; includes n=0 to fit the pattern
Knobs: complex constant c_n sets initial size and angle, with 0.5 and 45 degree examples
c0 is the average of the drawing; every rotating term averages to zero
Multiply by e^(-n...) to freeze vector n, then average kills the rest (smartphone-for-child joke)
General c_n formula read as freeze-then-average; how renders use SVG and numeric sums, 101 vectors
Back to step function; coefficients as exercise
Exponentials for linear differential equations recur; further reading links

theory: The video earns each symbol by giving it a physical job: rotating arrows come first, e^(it) arrives as shorthand for them, and the coefficient formula arrives as a two-step action on the drawing. Widening the problem to complex functions is sold as simplifying, with the real-valued case demoted to a special case.
velocity: Scene builder: render the finished complex phenomenon first, with a zoom to the smallest components, before any definition
Voice: when presenting a formula, narrate it as an ordered procedure applied to the on-screen object
Orchestrator: allow an explicit generalize-to-simplify beat, and say why widening helps
Learner model: track which rigor questions were deferred and offer them as optional deep dives
Evals: check notation is introduced as shorthand for a visible object, with its reason stated
